questions.question: In a series circuit, how does the voltage across each component relate to the total voltage of the battery?
options: The voltage across each component adds up to the total voltage of the battery.
Each component has the exact same voltage as the entire battery regardless of how many there are.
The component closest to the positive terminal receives all of the battery's voltage.
The total voltage of the battery is multiplied by the number of components in the circuit.

questions.question: Three 1.5 V electrical cells are connected together in series to form a battery. What is the total voltage of this battery?
What is the primary function of a battery in a complete electrical circuit?
options: It continuously creates new electrons that travel through the circuit.
It pushes electric charge (electrons) one way around a complete circuit.
It attracts positive protons to move through the metal wiring.
It stores up electric current until the circuit switch is turned off.

questions.question: What happens to the electrons throughout a circuit at the exact moment it is turned on?
options: Electrons everywhere in the circuit start moving at the same time.
Electrons start moving near the battery first, then gradually reach the rest of the wire.
Electrons at the switch move first, while those inside the bulb stay still.
Electrons move one by one from the positive terminal around to the negative terminal.

questions.question: How fast do individual electrons typically travel through a wire in a powered circuit?
options: At the speed of light.
At several kilometres per second.
At a moderate pace of a few metres per second.
Slowly, at a speed of just a few millimetres each second.

questions.question: Why does a faulty filament bulb stop current from flowing through a circuit?
options: The glass envelope absorbs all electrical charge.
The filament inside the bulb is broken, creating a gap in the path.
The metal contacts on the bulb lose their negative charge.
The wire inside the bulb automatically transforms into an insulator.

questions.question: If a series circuit contains one faulty component that stops it working, how can the remaining components be made to work again?
options: By using a wire to bypass the faulty component.
By connecting a second battery next to the faulty component.
By reversing the battery connections in the circuit.
By placing an insulating barrier inside the faulty component.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes a series circuit?
options: It is a circuit containing multiple independent loops for current to flow.
It is an electric circuit with one complete loop from one end of a battery to the other end.
It is a circuit that only operates when connected to mains electricity.
It is a circuit where current flows in two opposite directions simultaneously.

questions.question: How does an ammeter affect the electric current in a circuit when it is connected to take a reading?
options: It decreases the current significantly to protect the circuit components.
It measures the current flowing through it without affecting the current in the circuit.
It doubles the electric current passing through the main loop.
It converts all electric current into potential difference.

questions.question: What standard unit is used to measure electric current?
options: Volts (V)
Amps (A)
Ohms (Ω)
Joules (J)

questions.question: In a simple series circuit with two bulbs, how does the current near the battery compare to the current between the bulbs?
options: The current is higher near the battery than between the bulbs.
The current is lower near the battery than between the bulbs.
The current is zero between the bulbs because the energy was used.
The current in a series circuit is the same everywhere.

questions.question: What happens to the current in a series circuit when an extra component is added to the loop?
options: Adding a component changes the current everywhere, on both sides of the component.
The current decreases only on the side of the component closest to the negative terminal.
The current increases before the new component and decreases after it.
The current remains completely unchanged throughout the entire circuit.

questions.question: Which term is commonly used as another name for potential difference?
options: Electric current
Resistance
Voltage
Electrostatic charge

questions.question: How should a voltmeter be connected to measure the voltage across a circuit component?
options: Directly inside the main single loop alongside the component.
Across the terminals of the component.
Connected only to the positive terminal of the battery.
In between the cells inside the battery holder.

questions.question: What happens when two objects with opposite electric charges are brought near each other?
options: They attract each other.
They repel each other.
They lose their electric charges instantly.
They exert no force on each other.

questions.question: What happens when two objects with the same electric charge are brought close together?
options: They attract each other.
They repel each other.
They cancel each other out to become neutral.
They start generating electric current.

questions.question: What are the negatively charged particles inside atoms called?
options: Protons
Neutrons
Electrons
Ions

questions.question: Why is it difficult to build up a static electric charge on metal objects by rubbing them?
options: Metals do not contain any subatomic charges.
Metals immediately destroy any static charge that touches them.
Electric charge flows through metals, preventing charge from building up.
Friction cannot move electrons between any metal surfaces.

questions.question: When an electric circuit is switched off, what is true about the electric charges in the wires and components?
options: All electric charges disappear until the circuit is switched back on.
There are electric charges in all atoms of the wires and components, even when it is not turned on.
Electric charges return inside the battery and leave the wires empty.
Only positive charges remain in the wires when the circuit is off.

questions.question: How should wires be drawn in a clear, accurate circuit diagram?
options: As freehand curves with gaps to show where charge enters.
Using a ruler for clarity, with no gaps that would indicate a break in the circuit.
As double parallel lines representing both sides of the wire.
As dotted lines to show that electrical charge is invisible.
